*All Out (2021)* was the **third annual** event in All Elite Wrestling's (AEW) **All Out** pay-per-view (PPV) chronology. It took place on **September 5, 2021**, at the **Now Arena** in Hoffman Estates, Illinois (a suburb of Chicago). The event was a major success for AEW, featuring high-profile matches, shocking moments, and significant storyline developments.

---

### **Key Details**
- **Date:** September 5, 2021
- **Venue:** Now Arena (Hoffman Estates, Illinois)
- **Attendance:** ~10,000 (sold out)
- **Buyrate:** One of AEW's highest-grossing PPVs at the time (exact numbers not disclosed).
- **Main Event:** **Kenny Omega (c) vs. Christian Cage** for the **AEW World Championship**
- **Other Major Matches:**
  - **CM Punk vs. Darby Allin** (Punk’s first AEW match)
  - **Chris Jericho vs. MJF** (Jericho’s "Labors of Jericho" challenge)
  - **Bryan Danielson vs. Kenny Omega** (for a future title shot)
  - **The Young Bucks (c) vs. Lucha Brothers (Penta El Zero Miedo & Rey Fénix)** for the **AEW World Tag Team Championships** (Steel Cage Match)
  - **Dr. Britt Baker, D.M.D. (c) vs. Kris Statlander** for the **AEW Women’s World Championship**

---

### **Full Match Card & Results**
*(Winners in **bold**)*

1. **Pre-Show (Buy-In) Matches:**
   - **Jurassic Express (Jungle Boy & Luchasaurus) & Marko Stunt** def. **The Hardy Family Office (Private Party & Matt Hardy)** (6-Man Tag Team Match)
   - **Miro (c)** def. **Fuego Del Sol** to retain the **AEW TNT Championship** (Squash match)
   - **Paul Wight** def. **QT Marshall** (Singles Match)

2. **Main Card:**
   - **CM Punk** def. **Darby Allin** (Singles Match)
   - **Jon Moxley & Eddie Kingston** def. **Minoru Suzuki & Lance Archer** (Tag Team Match)
   - **Dr. Britt Baker, D.M.D. (c)** def. **Kris Statlander** to retain the **AEW Women’s World Championship** (Singles Match)
   - **Lucha Brothers (Penta El Zero Miedo & Rey Fénix)** def. **The Young Bucks (Matt & Nick Jackson) (c)** to win the **AEW World Tag Team Championships** (Steel Cage Match)
   - **Chris Jericho** def. **MJF** (Singles Match – "Labors of Jericho" challenge)
   - **Bryan Danielson** def. **Kenny Omega** (Singles Match – Winner gets a future AEW World Title shot)
   - **Kenny Omega (c)** def. **Christian Cage** to retain the **AEW World Championship** (Singles Match)

---

### **Major Storylines & Highlights**

#### **1. CM Punk’s AEW Debut & Match vs. Darby Allin**
- **CM Punk** made his **long-awaited AEW debut** at *The First Dance* (August 20, 2021) on *Dynamite*, ending his **7-year WWE hiatus**.
- He **challenged Darby Allin** to a match at All Out, which became one of the most hyped debuts in wrestling history.
- The match was **highly praised** for its storytelling, with Punk winning clean in his first AEW match.
- Post-match, **Punk cut a scathing promo** about his past, the wrestling business, and his future in AEW, setting up future feuds.

#### **2. The Young Bucks vs. Lucha Brothers (Steel Cage Match)**
- The **Lucha Brothers (Penta & Fénix)** had been feuding with **The Young Bucks** for months, with the Bucks’ **heel turn** (as part of The Elite) adding fuel to the fire.
- The match was **brutal**, featuring **high-risk spots** (including a **Canadian Destroyer** off the cage) and **blood** (Penta busted open).
- The Lucha Brothers **won the titles**, marking their first major championship in AEW.
- Post-match, **The Dark Order** (led by Evil Uno) **attacked The Young Bucks**, leading to a future feud.

#### **3. Kenny Omega vs. Christian Cage (AEW World Title Match)**
- **Christian Cage** debuted in AEW in **March 2021** and quickly rose up the ranks, earning a title shot at All Out.
- **Kenny Omega** (the **heel champion**) retained after **interference from Don Callis** and **The Good Brothers (Karl Anderson & Doc Gallows)**.
- The match was **technically strong** but overshadowed by the **post-match angle** where **Bryan Danielson (formerly Daniel Bryan in WWE) made his AEW debut** and **challenged Omega to a match**.

#### **4. Bryan Danielson’s AEW Debut & Match vs. Kenny Omega**
- **Bryan Danielson** (formerly **Daniel Bryan** in WWE) **shocked the wrestling world** by debuting at All Out after Omega’s match.
- He **challenged Omega to an immediate match**, which Omega accepted.
- The match was **a technical masterpiece**, with Danielson winning via **submission** (LeBell Lock).
- This set up **Danielson’s future AEW World Title pursuits** and his **feud with Adam Page**.

#### **5. Chris Jericho vs. MJF ("Labors of Jericho")**
- **MJF** had been **tormenting Jericho** for months, forcing him to complete **"Labors"** (challenges) to earn a match.
- Jericho **finally defeated MJF** in a **grudge match**, but MJF **revealed he had a "contract"** that allowed him to **choose his next opponent** (later revealed to be **Darius Martin of Top Flight**).
- This led to **MJF’s eventual alliance with Wardlow** and his **rise as a top heel**.

#### **6. Britt Baker vs. Kris Statlander (AEW Women’s Title Match)**
- **Dr. Britt Baker, D.M.D.** (the **heel champion**) defended against **Kris Statlander** in a **hard-hitting match**.
- Baker **retained** after **interference from Rebel** and a **curb stomp** on the steel steps.
- This match **elevated Statlander** and solidified Baker as the **top women’s star in AEW**.

#### **7. Miro’s TNT Title Reign Continues**
- **Miro** (formerly Rusev in WWE) was in the **middle of a dominant TNT Title reign**.
- He **squashed Fuego Del Sol** in a **short match**, continuing his **undefeated streak**.
- This led to his **future feud with Sammy Guevara**.

---

### **Post-Event Fallout & Long-Term Impact**
1. **CM Punk’s AEW Career Begins**
   - Punk’s **debut match** was a **huge success**, but his **post-match promo** (where he called out **Hangman Page, Colt Cabana, and WWE**) led to **backstage heat** and a **future suspension** (after the **2022 "Brawl Out" incident**).
   - He would later **feud with MJF** and **team with The Elite** before his **2023 retirement** due to injury.

2. **Bryan Danielson’s AEW Run Takes Off**
   - Danielson’s **debut match** was **instantly legendary**, and he became a **top babyface** in AEW.
   - He **feuded with Adam Page** (leading to a **5-star classic at Full Gear 2021**) and later **joined the Blackpool Combat Club**.

3. **The Lucha Brothers’ Tag Title Reign**
   - Penta & Fénix **held the tag titles for 122 days** before losing them to **Jurassic Express** at *Dynamite: Beach Break 2022*.
   - They later **turned heel** and joined **The House of Black**.

4. **Kenny Omega’s Title Reign Continues**
   - Omega **retained against Christian** but was **challenged by Bryan Danielson, Adam Page, and Hangman Page** in the coming months.
   - He eventually **lost the title to Adam Page** at *Full Gear 2021*.

5. **MJF’s Rise to Main Event Status**
   - After losing to Jericho, MJF **became a top heel**, eventually **winning the AEW World Title** in 2022.
   - His **feud with CM Punk** in 2022-23 became one of AEW’s **biggest storylines**.

6. **The Dark Order’s Face Turn**
   - After **attacking The Young Bucks**, The Dark Order **became fan favorites** and feuded with **The Elite**.
   - This led to **Evil Uno’s retirement** and **John Silver & Alex Reynolds** becoming key players in AEW.

---

### **Critical Reception & Legacy**
- **All Out 2021** is **widely regarded as one of AEW’s best PPVs**, thanks to:
  - **CM Punk’s debut match** (a historic moment in wrestling).
  - **Bryan Danielson’s shocking debut** and **instant classic** with Omega.
  - **The Lucha Brothers vs. Young Bucks cage match** (a **5-star match** per Dave Meltzer).
  - **Strong in-ring action** across the card.
- The event **drew massive buyrates** and **solidified AEW as a major player** in the wrestling industry.
- It also **set up major storylines** for the rest of 2021 and into 2022, including:
  - **Adam Page’s rise to the AEW World Title**.
  - **The Blackpool Combat Club’s formation**.
  - **CM Punk’s feud with MJF**.
  - **The Elite’s civil war** (leading to *AEW x NJPW: Forbidden Door*).

---

### **Fun Facts & Trivia**
- This was **CM Punk’s first wrestling match in 7 years** (since his 2014 WWE departure).
- **Bryan Danielson’s debut** was **kept secret** until the moment he walked out.
- The **Steel Cage match** was **AEW’s first-ever cage match** and set a **new standard** for tag team wrestling.
- **Paul Wight (Big Show)** had his **first AEW match** at All Out, defeating QT Marshall.
- **Miro’s squash match** was **so dominant** that it became a meme ("Miro is the TNT Champion").
- **Kris Statlander’s match** was **praised for its physicality**, proving she could hang with the best in AEW.

---

### **Final Verdict**
*All Out 2021* was a **landmark event** for AEW, **delivering historic moments, dream matches, and long-term storytelling**. It **elevated multiple stars** (Punk, Danielson, MJF, Lucha Brothers) and **set the stage for AEW’s biggest year yet (2022)**.
